title: villa-X: Enhancing Latent Action Modeling in Vision-Language-Action Models
claim: Standard latent action models learn latents only from visual reconstruction; adding an auxiliary proprioceptive dynamics head grounds them in physical state and action.
layout: 2 panels split by a dashed vertical line, left-to-right data flow in each, (a) existing vs (b) ours, captions below
description: Two side-by-side block diagrams separated by a dashed vertical line. Panel (a), 'Existing Latent Action Model', shows yellow observation boxes o_t and o_{t+K} feeding a blue IDM box, which outputs a green latent z_t. The latent feeds upward into a blue FDM box, which also receives o_t through a long arrow and outputs a predicted frame ô_{t+K}. Panel (b), 'Our Latent Action Model', repeats this structure. It adds a lower branch: z_t flows down into a blue 'proprio FDM' box, which also takes the purple state q_t and a brown embodiment context c_e. It outputs rows of predicted states q̂ (purple) and actions â (pink). Color-coded rounded boxes mark data types. The eye goes to the new proprio FDM branch in (b).
caption: (a) A standard Latent Action Model (LAM) learns a latent action $z_t$ primarily through visual reconstruction, predicting a future frame $\hat{o}_{t+K}$ from the current frame $o_t$ and latent action $z_t$. (b) Our proposed model enhances this by adding a proprio-FDM. This auxiliary module predicts future robot states $\hat{q}_{t+1:t+K}$ and actions $\hat{a}_{t:t+K-1}$ conditioned on an embodiment context $c_e$, enabling the latent actions to be better grounded in physical dynamics.
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as a popular paradigm for learning robot manipulation policies that can follow language instructions and generalize to novel scenarios. Recent works have begun to explore the incorporation of latent actions, abstract representations of motion between two frames, into VLA pre-training. In this paper, we introduce villa-X, a novel Vision-Language-Latent-Action (ViLLA) framework that advances latent action modeling for learning generalizable robot manipulation policies. Our approach improves both how latent actions are learned and how they are incorporated into VLA pre-training. We demonstrate that villa-X can generate latent action plans in a zero-shot fashion, even for unseen embodiments and open-vocabulary symbolic understanding. This capability enables villa-X to achieve superior performance across diverse simulation tasks in SIMPLER and on two real-world robotic setups involving both gripper and dexterous hand manipulation. These results establish villa-X as a principled and scalable paradigm for learning generalizable robot manipulation policies. We believe it provides a strong foundation for future research.
